data.narrative:
Neura Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Reger, has raised $1.4B to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 9 private robotics firms at Series B–D stages and 1 public comparable, providing two independent triangulation methods.

Stage-progression analysis, applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yields $2.4B. This method uses the $1.4B total raised as a proxy baseline and reflects expected step-up economics to the next funding round. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), and others—produces a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer set reflects heterogeneous staging but consistent sector exposure.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.4B (floor) to $2.7B (ceiling), with a median of $2.0B. The stage-progression method supports the upper half of this range, while peer-median anchors the lower-to-middle segment. Key uncertainties include stage-specific revenue or EBITDA multiples not present in available data, and timing sensitivity given the wide peer valuation dispersion ($1.0B–$2.0B). The analysis is most robust at the $2.0B midpoint but should be stress-tested against company-specific growth and capital efficiency metrics.
